summary:
## Overview

This guide details how to create a replica of Ghost's mask from *Modern Warfare 2* without using 3D printing or sculpting. The process relies on **papercraft templates**, which are then hardened and finished with common workshop materials to create a durable, game-accurate prop.

## Required Materials & Software

- **Software**: Pepakura Viewer
- **Templates**: Provided `.pdo` file
- **Base**: Hard paper
- **Adhesives**: Standard glue (for paper), Hot glue (for supports), Wood glue (for hardening)
- **Finishing**: Wood filler, Sandpaper
- **Paints**: Primer, White spray paint, Black & Brown acrylic/spray paint (for weathering)
- **Sealer**: Clear coat

## Step-by-Step Build Process

1.  **Template Assembly**: Print the templates on hard paper, cut them out, and assemble them using **Pepakura Viewer** as a 3D guide.
2.  **Hardening**: Apply multiple coats of **wood glue** over the entire paper mask to make it hard and durable. Add internal supports with hot glue to maintain its shape.
3.  **Smoothing**: Cover the mask with **wood filler** to hide the papercraft facets and create a smooth, bone-like surface.
4.  **Sanding & Detailing**: Sand the dried wood filler until the surface is completely smooth. Use a sharp tool to **carve details** like cracks before painting.
5.  **Priming & Painting**: Apply two coats of **primer**, followed by a base coat of white paint. Let it dry completely.
6.  **Weathering**: Create a wash by mixing **black paint and water**. Apply it to the mask and quickly wipe it off with a cloth or tissue to create a dirty look. Repeat with brown paint for more depth.
7.  **Final Details**: Carefully paint the two white vertical lines. Weather these lines slightly to blend them in. 
8.  **Sealing**: Apply a thin layer of **clear coat** to protect the paint job and give the mask a finished look.

## Key Techniques & Tips

> [!TIP]
> **Working with Glue & Filler**: If wood glue or wood filler becomes too thick or sticky to work with, dip your fingers in a small amount of water to help smooth the application process.

> [!NOTE]
> **Sizing is Critical**: The initial mask size may not fit correctly. Be prepared to scale the template and create more than one version to find the perfect size for your face. The creator made three attempts.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Use the Right Paint**: Do not use poster paint for the base coat. It is not a suitable surface for weathering effects. Stick to acrylics or spray paints over a proper primer for the best results.

## Introduction: Making a Better Ghost Mask

So today I've decided to make Ghost's mask from the new Modern Warfare 2, just because I'm sick of seeing this in the internet. I mean, just what the hell are this? Was that supposed to be Ghost? Because this actually looks like if Ghost and Riot had a baby. That was actually a bad example, sorry. Anyways, let's just jump right to the video.

## Templates and Software Setup

You can find the templates in the description of this video. First things first is I glue the template on the hard paper and then cut it out after it dries. Here it is all dried up. And just basically at this point you are just going to watch me build a whole mask with an epic transition.

Actually, before I forgot, you're going to have to download a software called Pepakura and a PDO file, both in the description of this video. You need to open the PDO file inside Pepakura in order to view where the pieces are going to connect. And by the way, I made it, so don't try to steal it. For that was a pretty bad Ghost impression, to be honest.

## Assembling and Sizing the Mask

This may seem like it only took me 30 seconds to finish, but in reality it was actually my entire day.

So the mask is 90% finished, but there's only just one problem. The mask I initially made was too big for my face, so I decided to create another one. However, this time it turned out to be a little small. Finally, the third mask I made was just the right size.

## Reinforcing the Mask with Wood Glue

So I decided not to record the teeth part due to my laziness and also I inserted some supports inside the skull so it can maintain the shape that I wanted. So here I am applying some white glue to the mask to make it more hard and thick. That's what she said. And also when my fingers get sticky applying the wood glue, I will just dip them in water to make the glue more smoother. And I'm going to speed this up now.

And now that the application of wood glue is finished, I'm going to wait for it to dry and then we can proceed to apply some wood filler. And also I filled the back of the mask with some hot glue in order to really maintain its shape.

## Creating a Smooth Surface with Wood Filler

So this is the part where the mask will look really good. When we apply the wood filler to the mask, it will make the surface smooth, especially after we sand it. And just like with the wood glue, if the filler gets too hard, I will apply a little bit of water to soften it.

So here it is after applying the wood filler. The next step now is to sand it down.

## Sanding, Detailing, and Priming

So after doing a lot of filling and sanding, here is the result. I've also made this crack here by using a sharp tool like this one to carve into the surface of the wood filler.

Next thing I did was apply two coats of primer, and the result was amazing. So apparently I made a mistake with this part because I accidentally used poster paint instead of acrylic. So I need to remove the paint on it and apply a primer again. And I also end up just using spray paint.

## Weathering Technique: Black Wash

After applying white paint, it is now the time to make the mask look dirty. So the first thing I did was mix black paint and water together and then I applied it to the mask. After that, I rub it with a tissue paper or cloth, which I prefer, before the paint dries. Just repeat the process and you're good to go.

## Adding Brown Weathering and Line Guides

So in this part, I'm now using a brown color to add more dirtiness to the mask.

So in this part, I'm now making a guide on where to put the two white lines of Ghost's mask correctly.

## Painting Details and Applying Clear Coat

After I'm done drawing the guide, it is now time to paint.

Apparently the two lines were too clean, so we needed to make it dirty.

The mask is looking pretty good now, and all we just needed to do is apply a thin layer of clear coat.

## Final Result and Conclusion

Here it is, the mask. It is almost finished, just a few minor details left to add, such as the strings in Ghost's mask and especially the balaclava. So any thoughts?

In my opinion, this is by far the most accurate looking Ghost mask on the internet without the use of 3D printing or sculpting. The template was actually based on the game files that I downloaded on the Internet, thanks to the person who ripped it off from the game. Overall, I'm really happy with how it turned out in the end. It exceeded my expectations. And to be honest, I also made some crappy Ghost masks before this one. So yeah, that's all. Thanks for watching and remember, stay frosty.

Oh, and also watch the part two of this video.
